cohort: 869 medical students who completed their OB/GYN clerkship between 2014 and 2022 at a single United States allopathic medical school.
finding: While no overall differences in hands-on delivery experience were found based on medical student gender or URM status, subgroup analysis revealed that URM and non-URM male students participated in fewer vaginal deliveries compared to non-URM female peers.
mod_finding: URM male students participated in fewer vaginal deliveries and total deliveries compared to non-URM female students, and non-URM male students participated in fewer vaginal deliveries than non-URM female peers.
